subject.title: In-turn background work (Workflow / run_in_background / Workflow-backed skills) is SIGKILLed at the turn boundary under the claude-cli runtime

question: Should claude-cli background work that claims to outlive a turn be supported with a bounded durable lifecycle, or explicitly denied and surfaced as unsupported under OpenClaw?
rationale: The source confirms the cleanup and process-tree kill path, but the permanent behavior changes process lifetime, orphan prevention, user-visible completion delivery, and the boundary with Claude Code native tools.

options.title: Adopt bounded longwork contract
options.body: Detect pending claude-cli-owned background work, preserve or detach it only within a bounded lifecycle, snapshot origin delivery, and surface forced cleanup as a typed failure.

options.title: Deny unsupported native background work
options.body: Expand docs, tool policy, and diagnostics so unsupported Claude native background affordances fail visibly instead of launching work that cannot survive the turn.

options.title: Defer to run-lifecycle umbrella
options.body: Keep this as a linked requirement under the broader run-lifecycle design issue, but do not close it until that umbrella explicitly owns Workflow/background delivery.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded longwork contract
recommendation.body: Detect pending claude-cli-owned background work, preserve or detach it only within a bounded lifecycle, snapshot origin delivery, and surface forced cleanup as a typed failure.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus introduced the warm Claude CLI live-session model and owns the broad run-lifecycle reliability design issue that overlaps this decision.
